newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission reorganises after BSE crisis.
newsitem.headline: Commission reorganises after BSE crisis.

text.p: The European Commission, rocked by allegations of incompetence over its handling of the BSE crisis, agreed a shake-up on Wednesday to help prevent and deal more efficiently with food health crises.
"The Commission thinks that its activities on food health should be made more efficient, more transparent and more balanced," it said in a statement.
Under the plans, agreed a week before the European Parliament discusses an inquiry committee report on the crisis, Commissioner Emma Bonino will take responsibility for food health issues.
Her consumer directorate general DG XXIV will be renamed the directorate for consumer policy and health protection.
All relevant committees will be attached to a new directorate, rather than different directorates and directorate generals as now.
A special management committee grouping the presidents of the different sectoral committees will be set up to ensure transparency and coherence between them.
Horst Reichenbach, former chef de cabinet for German Commissioner Monika Wulf-Mathies, will take over as head of DG XXIV.

Three principles have underpinned the Commission reshuffle -- the need to separate the services drawing up legislation and those responsible for scientific consultation; to separate those responsible for drawing up legislation and those responsible for enforcing it; and strengthening transparency and accessibility of information.
A group of commissioners for food safety, headed by Commission President Jacques Santer, will be set up to ensure political control of the issue.
The office of inspection of animal and plant health will be moved from the agriculture directorate DGVI to DG XXIV.
The Commission has undertaken to come up with proposals within two months to improve the functioning of the sectoral committees.
A special body will also be set up to assess food health risks and carry out checks.
